item.text: The source compiles, but the runtime invocation didn’t pick up the packaged class as expected. I’m checking the generated class layout and classpath assumptions before making any more code changes.

I found a real design issue in the new traverser: it keeps traversal state on the instance, so repeated calls on the same object accumulate results incorrectly. I’m fixing that by making the traverser reusable and moving per-run state into a fresh session object.

I’m doing one follow-up cleanup in the graph base class as part of the same pass: removing the now-unused protected adjacency-view accessor, since storage ownership is already handled by `AdjacencyLists`.
The cleanup patch missed the current file shape. I’m reading the base class and applying the exact change against the current contents.

The reusable-traverser fix is in. I’m recompiling and running the packaged app again, and I’ll do a quick behavioral check that two traversals from the same traverser no longer accumulate stale state.

I continued the refactor by moving the demo entry point into [app/BreadthFirstSearchApp.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/004_breadth_first_search/app/BreadthFirstSearchApp.java:1) and replacing the static utility-style BFS class with [graph/traversal/BreadthFirstTraverser.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/004_breadth_first_search/graph/traversal/BreadthFirstTraverser.java:9). That gives the codebase a cleaner package boundary between app wiring and traversal logic.

I also fixed a design bug introduced by the earlier refactor: traversal state is no longer stored on the traverser instance. Each call now creates a fresh private `TraversalSession`, so reusing the same `BreadthFirstTraverser` won’t accumulate stale `visited` or traversal-order state across calls.
